official_measurement_examples.name: Planning consultation trigger
official_measurement_examples.fact: In England planning authorities must contact DfT and the relevant network operator where development could materially increase the volume or change the character of traffic using a level crossing.

official_measurement_examples.name: ORR permission limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR explicitly states it does not approve or grant permission for new or reinstated level crossings, although it may provide safety views in TWA processes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Legal crossing right
official_measurement_examples.fact: A proposer must separately establish the legal right to cross the railway, usually through an enabling Act or Order; ORR has no role in granting that land right.

official_measurement_examples.name: TWA current transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: DfT updated TWA guidance on 18 February 2026 following the Planning and Infrastructure Act 2025, including changes to procedure and deemed marine-licence handling for eligible applications.

official_measurement_examples.name: TWA and planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: A TWA order can authorise railway or tramway works, but planning permission may be included or sought separately depending on the scheme; a TWA application is not itself final permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Level crossing order scope
official_measurement_examples.fact: Level Crossing Orders specify safety/protection arrangements at crossings; they do not establish parcel ownership, development yield or a general right to create new development access.

official_measurement_examples.name: Dynamic risk
official_measurement_examples.fact: ORR says crossing risk changes with train service, road traffic, user behaviour and other conditions, so a historic risk assessment must not be treated as permanently current.

official_measurement_examples.name: Asset protection role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Network Rail asset-protection engagement manages third-party works affecting railway infrastructure and is separate from planning permission, TWA authority, crossing rights and land ownership.

core_rules: level crossing proximity is not automatic planning refusal
material traffic change can trigger statutory consultation
ORR does not grant new level crossing permission
ORR safety view is not planning permission
legal right to cross railway is separately established
level crossing order is not land ownership evidence
TWA application is not final TWA order
TWA order and planning permission remain distinct where applicable
asset protection engagement is not planning permission
railway risk assessment must retain date and operating context
crossing closure preference is risk policy not parcel development prohibition
railway geometry does not determine development yield
public/private right of way questions remain separate from ORR safety role
TWA marine/licence integration does not erase other required consents
no parcel rail-access clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official ORR, DfT/GOV.UK and Network Rail sources checked on 2026-07-26. February-July 2026 TWA and level-crossing risk context was retained with consultation, safety, order, land-right, planning and asset-protection separation; no parcel promotion.
